title: Making a Skincare Store Easier to Shop
description: Reviewed the path from homepage to product page, found five places where shoppers could lose confidence, and turned them into a clear seven-step fix list.
seoTitle: Making a Skincare Store Easier to Shop
seoDescription: A project that reviews an online skincare store from a shopper's point of view and turns five buying problems into a clear, evidence-backed fix list.
teamSize: Solo review for the store owner
constraints: The review used public pages only, without the store's private dashboard, sales reports, customer information, or website admin access.
The live store could not be changed during the review, so every recommendation needed enough evidence and detail for the owner to act on later.
The store sells skincare products, so recommendations about trust and product claims had to stay careful and avoid promising health outcomes.
The report could show what made shopping harder, but it could not claim a sales increase before the owner made and measured the changes.
problem: An online skincare store owner wanted to know what might be stopping more visitors from buying.
Shoppers were being asked to choose premium botanical oils without enough help connecting unfamiliar ingredient names to their own skin or hair concerns.
The public store also had an empty skin-assessment path, six of 11 visible products out of stock, unanswered product questions, and slow mobile pages.
solution: Followed the shopping path from the homepage through the skin assessment, product list, and a representative product page on desktop and mobile.
Used screenshots, stock counts, speed checks, and 13 reference sources to separate visible shopping problems from questions that required private store data.
Built a report website with five findings, seven fixes in the order I would tackle them, four clear screenshot examples, a shorter summary page, and 11 questions for a deeper follow-up.
result: Turned a broad request to improve sales into a concrete explanation of where shoppers could get stuck and what the owner should fix first.
Put the empty skin assessment, unclear product fit, sold-out inventory, unanswered product questions, and mobile speed into one practical order of work.
Gave each fix a result to watch, such as assessment completion, product-page visits, add-to-cart rate, checkout starts, email signups, or mobile sales.
Kept the outcome honest: the work proves a thorough review and useful report, not an increase in sales that has not yet been measured.
deliveryHighlights: Shipped a report website with 5 findings, 7 fixes in order, 4 screenshot examples, 13 source links, and 11 questions for a second review using the store's real numbers.
Generated a shorter executive summary from the same report content so the two versions stay consistent.
Checked the homepage and a representative product page on desktop and mobile; the reported scores were 91 and 90 on desktop, compared with 63 and 60 on mobile.
Kept the report out of search results and left private store data, account access, and unverified sales claims out of the public case study.
